entries.title: EVOKE
entries.summary: A fashion brand system that treats invoices, tags, receipts, and cards as one language. Cream stock + ink, a modular interlocking motif, and mono for all transactional text — taste through constraint, not decoration.

screenshots.caption: Full system — invoice, cards, receipt strip, thank-you notes, product tag

audit.observation: Every touchpoint shares motif, type pair, and palette. Remove the logo and the shapes still read as EVOKE.
Wide display for the wordmark; mono for prices, SKUs, and contact. Two jobs, two voices.
The puzzle-block motif is the signature. Generic sans + stock mockups would not survive the brand test.
Works as print/stationery. A live product UI would still need a motion and interaction layer.

intentions.title: One motif, many surfaces
intentions.explanation: Significance comes from repeating one invented shape across invoice, tag, and card until it becomes identity — not from adding more ornaments.

intentions.title: Mono as honesty
intentions.explanation: Monospace on prices and contact feels archival and precise. It signals craft over marketing gloss.

intentions.title: Cream instead of white
intentions.explanation: Warm stock reads premium and print-aware. Pure white would flatten the system into generic digital.

takeaways: Invent one modular shape and run it across every artifact.
Pair one loud display face with one quiet mono — stop at two.
If the first viewport could belong to another brand after removing the logo, the motif is too weak.

entries.title: Client Folders
entries.summary: A client file taxonomy drawn as a tree of pastel folders. Not a UI screen — a process poster that makes invisible project structure feel physical and memorable.

screenshots.caption: Full tree — root client name into LEGAL, DISCOVERY, BRAND, FINAL FILES

audit.observation: Four pillars + nested leaves. Instantly scannable for freelancers and studios.
Actual folder icons + soft shadows make process feel tangible instead of a spreadsheet.
Lavender root, lime categories, pink leaves — depth by hue, not by more labels.
As a site section it would need interaction. As a taste reference for clarity, it is gold.

intentions.title: Make process visible
intentions.explanation: Taste is not only final screens. Showing how work is organized signals professionalism and care.

intentions.title: Hue equals depth
intentions.explanation: Color encodes hierarchy so the eye understands nesting without reading every label twice.

takeaways: Document your own project IA as a designed artifact, not a Drive dump.
Use 3 hue bands for 3 hierarchy levels — never rainbow spam.

entries.title: Fitness Flow
entries.summary: A fitness-app user flow that looks designed, not dumped from a whiteboard tool. Cursive title, black screen nodes, lime action parallelograms, and red/green yes-no paths.

screenshots.caption: Full flow — onboarding through Home hub to Workouts, Coaching, Challenges

audit.observation: Blue forward / red return paths + green/red dots make happy path vs backtrack obvious at a glance.
Black pills = screens, lime parallelograms = inputs/actions, diamonds = decisions. Consistent grammar.
Hand-script title + beige ground elevate a document usually left ugly. Process can have presence.
Side notes help but can crowd; best when parked near the node they explain.

intentions.title: Grammar before decoration
intentions.explanation: Uniqueness here is a consistent shape language for logic — not stickers or gradients.

intentions.title: Stack equals collection
intentions.explanation: Stacked shadows on Workouts / Exercise communicate list-of-items without icons.

takeaways: Give every UX diagram a designed title treatment and a limited color grammar.
Encode Yes/No in both line color and node color — redundancy helps scanning.

entries.title: Vijaya Bank
entries.summary: A banking-app redesign presented as a numbered screen story (01–05) with yellow brand discs, sitemap callouts, and a written 5-step transfer flow. Case study as designed object.

screenshots.alt: Vijaya Bank UI case study board
screenshots.caption: Screens 01–05 with annotations and main-navigation sitemap

audit.observation: Splash to Login to Home to Cards to Transfer reads as a journey, not a random gallery.
Yellow square bullets + short prose explain why, not just what.
Home sprouts a sitemap tree — architecture made visible beside the UI.
Many devices + lines risk clutter on small viewports; works best as a poster or wide desktop.

intentions.title: Show the path, not just the pixels
intentions.explanation: Significance comes from explaining navigation and transfer steps — proving thinking, not only polish.

intentions.title: Brand as field
intentions.explanation: Yellow discs behind phones turn brand color into atmosphere instead of a tiny logo corner.

takeaways: Number your case-study screens and connect them with flow arrows.
Park a sitemap next to the home screen so IA is not buried in a PDF.

entries.title: Too-Doo
entries.summary: A process page for a personal-assistant app: (1) ANALYZE as a user mind-map, (2) IDEATE as eight hand-drawn wireframes on a dot grid. Thinking made visible.

screenshots.caption: Mind map + sketch wireframes on notebook ground

audit.observation: Shows messy thinking before polish — rare and trustworthy in portfolios.
Numbered phases with one-line briefs. Clear job per block.
Hand wireframes on dots feel human; pure Figma frames would kill the spell.
Stops at ideate — a final UI strip would complete the story.

intentions.title: Process is the product of taste
intentions.explanation: Uniqueness here is willingness to show analysis and sketches — most portfolios hide the kitchen.

intentions.title: Dot grid equals studio
intentions.explanation: The notebook texture frames the work as craft, not a slide deck.

takeaways: Add an Analyze / Ideate strip before polished mockups in case studies.
Keep early wireframes hand-feel — do not over-clean them.

entries.title: 1-Bit Portraits
entries.summary: Sixteen head-and-shoulder avatars in strict black/white pixel language. Diversity through silhouette and accessory — not through color.

screenshots.caption: 4x4 avatar system — glasses, hoods, beards, caps within one bit-depth

audit.observation: One bit depth forces invention. Checker dither stands in for gray.
Same crop, same outline weight, same scale — a true set, not 16 random doodles.
Accessories and haircuts carry identity. Readable at tiny sizes.

intentions.title: Limits create signature
intentions.explanation: Taste often means refusing more colors. The set is memorable because it is strict.

intentions.title: Uniform frame, varied soul
intentions.explanation: Same composition rules + different features = collection energy.

takeaways: Try a one-bit or two-color illustration lane for a section of the portfolio.
When building a set, lock crop and stroke first — then vary content.

entries.title: FLYQ
entries.summary: A commercial real-estate site concept where each section is a giant rounded card with folder-index tabs. Pastel grounds + line art + big numbers.

screenshots.caption: Five section cards — white, blue, pink, mint, yellow — shared tab chrome

audit.observation: Folder tabs make IA physical. Active tab color matches card ground.
Each chapter owns a pastel — memory without reading labels twice.
Photo + line illustration + stats coexist because borders and type hierarchy hold them.
Very large radii — soft brand. Clashes with hard brutalist refs elsewhere; know when to choose.

intentions.title: Tabs as identity
intentions.explanation: The folder chrome is the uniqueness — not a standard sticky nav.

intentions.title: Color per chapter
intentions.explanation: Pastels encode section memory so scrolling feels like flipping a physical binder.

takeaways: Give each major portfolio chapter a color field and a shared chrome pattern.
Pair one photo with one line illustration — not a collage pile.

entries.title: Jornada Analog
entries.summary: Event poster as stacked physical documents on pure black: manila tab, perforated white sheet, blue sticky, graph scrap, binder clip. Analog-brutalist archival taste.

screenshots.caption: Layered dossier — clip, sticky, perforated sheet, grid scrap, footer logos

audit.observation: Paper types organize info categories. Containers do the IA work.
Cream dossier on black void feels precious and gallery-ready.
Bold slashed-O display + mono for addresses/dates — technical + ceremonial.
Needs CSS layering and assets; flat cards would lose the point.

intentions.title: Physical metaphor as structure
intentions.explanation: Clips and paper stocks are not decoration — they are information containers.

intentions.title: Void as pedestal
intentions.explanation: Black ground makes the dossier feel collected and significant.

takeaways: Layer 2–3 paper surfaces for dense info pages instead of one flat card.
Put transactional data in mono; keep the headline ceremonial.

entries.title: Antoni Alison
entries.summary: A wall of yellow sticky notes with marker words (GASP, STUN, SPEECHLESS) and sparse sketches. Conceptual planning as the visual — huge empty gray field as confidence.

screenshots.caption: Asymmetric note cluster on gray — emotion words and doodles

audit.observation: Most of the canvas is empty. That emptiness is the taste.
Punchy handwritten copy beats polite portfolio filler.
Shadows under notes sell the object. Flat yellow rectangles would fail.
Mood piece — weak as a product IA doc, strong as brand attitude.

intentions.title: Empty as luxury
intentions.explanation: Leaving the right half blank signals confidence. Crowding would kill uniqueness.

intentions.title: Words as objects
intentions.explanation: Single emotive words on notes become graphic marks, not paragraphs.

takeaways: Protect large empty regions in at least one portfolio section.
Try handwritten or marker-feel type for a mood strip — not for body copy.

entries.title: Hinomaru Wave
entries.summary: The Japanese sun disc dissolving into a Great-Wave crest inside a thin black frame on textured paper. Conceptual graphic with one clever move — taste as idea, not as UI kit.

screenshots.alt: Hinomaru sun merging with Great Wave
screenshots.caption: Full composition — red field, wave foam, framed dissolving sun

audit.observation: One visual pun does the work of a paragraph. Memorable in one glance.
Red, cream, black line. Nothing else. Scarcity creates significance.
Paper grain keeps it from feeling like a flat vector sticker.

intentions.title: Idea over ornament
intentions.explanation: Uniqueness is the melt of sun into wave — a decision, not a filter pack.

intentions.title: Frame as anchor
intentions.explanation: The thin rectangle grounds fluid motion so the piece does not float away.

takeaways: Build at least one portfolio visual around a single conceptual move.
Add paper grain when a bold flat color risks feeling cheap.

entries.title: Blossom on Red
entries.summary: A slender blossom branch on a flat saturated red field. Organic detail vs digital plane — confidence through emptiness and one precise subject.

screenshots.alt: White blossoms on solid red background
screenshots.caption: Full frame — diagonal branch, two blooms, chroma void

audit.observation: One subject. Zero competing modules. Portfolio hero energy.
Delicate white petals need the aggressive red field to feel precious.
As a section background or interstitial it sings; as dense product UI it does not.

intentions.title: Chroma as identity
intentions.explanation: A single loud field color is a brand decision. Most portfolios fear it.

intentions.title: Organic vs flat
intentions.explanation: Real botanical detail against a digital plane creates modern East-Asian graphic tension.

takeaways: Try one full-bleed brand-color interstitial between case studies.
Let one image breathe — no badges, no chips, no floating labels.

entries.title: Dissolving Sun
entries.summary: A perfect red semicircle whose lower half breaks into vertical motion streaks on textured cream. Rising-sun motif reinvented with blur and grain.

screenshots.alt: Red sun dissolving into vertical streaks
screenshots.caption: Full frame — solid crest, blurred reflection bars, paper grain

audit.observation: Reads as sun-on-water without literal photography.
Grain unifies figure and ground — premium analog feel.
Blur as meaning, not as cheap transition. Translates well to hover/load states.

intentions.title: Transform a known symbol
intentions.explanation: Everyone knows the red circle. Significance comes from breaking it intentionally.

intentions.title: Effect with purpose
intentions.explanation: Motion blur is the metaphor for reflection — not a default CSS toy.

takeaways: When using effects (blur, grain, glitch), tie them to a metaphor.
Center one symbol; protect margins like a gallery mat.

entries.title: Dimension
entries.summary: AI coworker landing page with gradient sky atmosphere, frosted floating nav, and a live Morning Briefing preview. Product shown, not just claimed. ([dimension.dev](https://dimension.dev/))

screenshots.caption: Hero — split pitch + briefing preview, floating bottom dock

audit.observation: Right panel is a believable product surface (Steve's briefing). Trust builds instantly.
Sky gradient + grain beats flat SaaS blue. Mood is the differentiator.
Bottom floating dock clears the hero and feels app-native.
Glass + gradient is now common in AI SaaS — execution quality saves it, but uniqueness is thinner than print/brutalist refs.

intentions.title: Product as hero media
intentions.explanation: The briefing card is the brand image — no stock photos of smiling teams.

intentions.title: Feature list as theater
intentions.explanation: Vertical Morning Briefing / Catch Up switcher drives the preview, reducing scroll fatigue.

takeaways: Put a real product surface in the first viewport when the work is digital.
Steal atmosphere (gradient + grain), but invent a chrome pattern that is not default glass.

entries.title: Sofia Khegai
entries.summary: Creative producer portfolio that puts a custom geometric wordmark (khegai) at hero scale on black with bubblegum pink. Brand first — the name is the composition. ([khegai.com](https://khegai.com/?ref=minimal.gallery))

screenshots.caption: Hero — massive pink wordmark, condensed bio, outline pill filters

audit.observation: Remove nav and the page still belongs to Khegai. Name is the artwork.
Giant display vs tiny all-caps bio creates luxury hierarchy.
Two colors only. Loud and memorable.
Work lives below; first paint is identity. Recruiters who need proof fast must scroll.

intentions.title: Name as hero image
intentions.explanation: Uniqueness is typographic authorship. A template font would collapse the brand test.

intentions.title: Nav as cluster
intentions.explanation: Pill outline buttons in a corner replace boring top bars — boutique, not corporate.

takeaways: Make your name (or a coined word) a designed object at hero scale.
Limit the first viewport to brand + one short line + one CTA group.

entries.title: Boris Verks
entries.summary: Product-designer portfolio: headshot + giant all-caps intro, hairline sidebar, metric highlights, then a blue work-snippet stage. High information density with low visual noise. ([borisverks.com](https://www.borisverks.com/?ref=minimal.gallery))

screenshots.caption: Above the fold — portrait, manifesto type, sidebar, Jetraw snippet

audit.observation: Role, availability, proof bullets, and contact are immediate. Friction near zero.
Site stays ink/paper until work snippets explode in blue — controlled drama.
All-caps grotesk manifesto is confident; secondary grey line for open-to-work is smart hierarchy.
Can feel austere. The headshot is what keeps it human.

intentions.title: Evidence over ambience
intentions.explanation: Significance comes from checkmarked outcomes and named companies, not decorative hero art.

intentions.title: Color reserved for work
intentions.explanation: Monochrome chrome makes the product screenshot the only color event — hierarchy by scarcity.

takeaways: Put proof bullets (metrics, awards) next to the first project snippet.
Keep site chrome near-monochrome; spend color on the work itself.

entries.title: Rachel Chen
entries.summary: Product designer + engineer portfolio: elegant serif line ('who engineers.'), right-rail internship table (Notion, Bloomberg, 1Password…), then pastel project cards. Soft, precise, credible. ([rachelchen.tech](https://www.rachelchen.tech/?ref=minimal.gallery))

screenshots.caption: Hero — serif statement + year/company/role table + pastel card tops

audit.observation: Italic 'engineers.' sells the dual skillset in one word. Sharp.
Name-brand timeline lives in the hero — no click required.
Off-white + coral accent + pastel cards feel designed, not default dark-mode AI slop.
Many designer portfolios share this soft minimal language — execution is high, but motif uniqueness is quieter than Khegai/EVOKE.

intentions.title: Type encodes identity
intentions.explanation: Serif for the human statement, sans for the resume table — designer + engineer as typographic pairing.

intentions.title: Proof without shouting
intentions.explanation: Muted grey table of elite companies lets credentials whisper while the headline speaks.

takeaways: Put a compact experience table in the hero if credentials are a strength.
Use one italicized verb to lock your unique positioning.
